answer: An agent economy can counter Sybil attacks using graph-based trust propagation, bounding influence through random walks from trusted seeds. To emit a valid signal, an attacker must obtain inbound edges from authentic peers, incurring the verifiable cost of bilateral interaction history. Even at the zenith of compute scale, forged clusters cannot whisper false authority past graph bottlenecks. However, this approach disadvantages legitimate nascent agents lacking social capital.
